newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf pipelines operational after Thursday shuts.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf pipelines operational after Thursday shuts.

text.p: A trio of U.S. Gulf pipelines were forced to shut overnight Thursday after a Coast Guard patrol spotted two oil sheens, but the lines were operating again on Friday without incident, a Coast Guard official said.

Coast Guard officials in Morgan City, Louisiana said the Texaco Poseidon pipeline and Shell Oil Co's 24-inch pipeline are "on-line" again, and were not the cause of the what may have been a pipeline leak.
A third line, a 12-inch line operated by Forest Gas, is in the process of being repressurized, but has not yet been cleared of causing the possible leak.

"We know it was not a Texaco or a Shell pipeline, and if it's not Forest, then it was a natural event," said Lt. Dave Weimer, senior investigator in the Coast Guard marine safety office in Morgan City.

A Texaco spokesman said Poseidon was shut for 14 hours from early Thursday evening to Friday morning, shutting in 60,000 barrels of crude. Infrared inspections on the line did not show any leaks, the spokesman said.

On Thursday afternoon, an aviation check of Gulf waters revealed two sheens containing an estimated 1,500 barrels of oil. The oil spots were seen in the south Timbalier section of water, in block 207, Weimer said. "The sheens were seen due south of Houma, Louisiana, 40 miles off beach."
Subsequent overflights showed the sheens dissipating, Weimer said.
